title: Structural and Thermodynamic Insights into Competitive Binding of the EGR1 and Sp1 Zinc Finger Class of Transcription Factors with a GC-Rich DNA Motif.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过微秒级原子模拟结合结构生物信息学，揭示EGR1与Sp1锌指转录因子对GC-rich DNA基序的竞争性结合机制，聚焦TF-DNA互作界面、DNA形状特征与结合自由能，方法上采用MD模拟，高度契合本课题。
abstract: Transcriptional control of gene regulation in eukaryotes is primarily associated with the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to a particular motif sequence in genomic DNA, among the vast number of identical or highly similar sequences in the genome. The cooperative as well as competitive interactions among the paralogous TFs are believed to play an important role in this aspect to control precise gene regulatory functions. So far, the molecular mechanism of competitive TF binding is obscured, and due to a lack of molecular insights, it is difficult to predict how competitive interaction influences the genomic binding of individual TFs. Using microsecond atomistic simulations together with structural and functional bioinformatics data, here, we report the competitive binding nature of two biologically important zinc finger (ZF) class of pioneer TFs, namely, early growth response protein 1 (EGR1) and specificity protein 1* (Sp1), with highly similar GC-rich motif sequences. We show that the conformational entropy of protein and DNA components makes a substantial contribution in binding to a specific DNA motif and illustrate the roles of DNA shape features in competitive binding. The intrinsic shape features, along with local shape deformability of the DNA binding site motif, are found to facilitate sequence-specific recognition and binding of EGR1/Sp1 through the ZF domains by giving access to the base atoms of the specific bases along the grooves to form major contacts with the conserved residues in the canonical recognition positions in ZFs. Base-specific contacts of the functional key conserved charged residues of the ZFs in the DBD of EGR1/Sp1, along the major grooves of the DNA motif, further modulate the binding interactions, dynamics, and dissociation free energy. In general, this study provides microscopic insights into how the complex patterns of competitive TFs are intrinsically encoded in the DNA binding motif and help to design custom ZF nucleases for site-specific genome editing machinery.
abstract_zh: 真核生物中基因调控的转录控制主要与转录因子（TFs）结合基因组DNA中特定基序序列有关，尽管基因组中存在大量相同或高度相似的序列。旁系同源转录因子之间的协同及竞争性相互作用被认为在精确调控基因功能方面发挥重要作用。迄今为止，竞争性TF结合的分子机制尚不明确，且由于缺乏分子层面的见解，难以预测竞争性相互作用如何影响单个TF的基因组结合。利用微秒级原子模拟结合结构和功能生物信息学数据，我们在此报告了两种生物学重要的锌指（ZF）类先锋转录因子——即早期生长反应蛋白1（EGR1）和特异性蛋白1*（Sp1）——与高度相似的GC富集基序序列的竞争性结合特性。我们展示了蛋白质和DNA组分的构象熵在结合特定DNA基序中做出显著贡献，并阐明了DNA形状特征在竞争性结合中的作用。发现DNA结合位点基序的内在形状特征，连同局部形状可变形性，通过沿沟槽暴露特定碱基的碱基原子，促进EGR1/Sp1通过ZF结构域进行序列特异性识别和结合，从而与ZF中规范识别位置的保守残基形成主要接触。EGR1/Sp1 DBD中ZF功能关键保守带电残基沿DNA基序大沟的碱基特异性接触，进一步调节结合相互作用、动力学和解离自由能。总体而言，本研究提供了微观层面的见解，揭示了竞争性TF的复杂模式如何内在编码于DNA结合基序中，并有助于设计用于位点特异性基因组编辑机制的自定义ZF核酸酶。
